intro: A page of the Babylonian Talmud can look like a puzzle. There is a block of text in the middle. There are smaller columns wrapped around it. There are notes in tiny letters at the edges. In this unit you will learn how that page is built, who wrote each part, and how printers in Venice and Vilna set it in place.

Then you will learn how the words in the middle move. The Gemara asks questions, brings proofs, raises objections and gives answers. Sometimes it leaves a question open. You will meet the tools the rabbis used, like kal va-chomer and gezerah shavah, and famous pairs of voices, like Rav and Shmuel, Abaye and Rava.

By the end you will be able to find your way around a page, cite it the standard way, and trace the steps of a sugya. You will also be able to explain why the Talmud keeps the side that lost, and what its rulings protect, from the worker in the field to the person whose view was outvoted.
bigQuestion: How is a page of Talmud built, and how does its argument move from question to answer?

timeline.t: The Mishnah is arranged, tradition says by Judah the Prince
Rav comes to Babylonia; Shmuel teaches at Nehardea
Abaye and Rava debate in Pumbedita and Mahoza
The Babylonian Talmud takes its final shape, historians date
Rashi lives in Troyes, France, and writes his commentary
The Tosafists, Rashi's grandsons and students, add their notes
Daniel Bomberg prints the first full Talmud in Venice
The Romm press prints the Vilna Shas
The Schottenstein English edition begins to appear
The full Talmud goes online in English on Sefaria

words.d: the early rabbinic law code, arranged c. 200 CE, written mostly in Hebrew
the rabbis' recorded discussion of the Mishnah, written mostly in Aramaic
Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki (1040–1105), whose commentary sits on the inner margin of the page
"additions"; notes by Rashi's grandsons and students, on the outer margin
a leaf of the Talmud, with two sides, a and b
one complete discussion in the Gemara
an objection or difficulty raised against a claim
an answer that resolves an objection
"let it stand"; a question left unresolved
an argument from a lesser case to a greater one
linking two laws because the Torah uses the same word in both
a teaching of the tannaim left outside the Mishnah

test.q: What sits at the center of a Vilna Talmud page?
test.why: The center block holds the Mishnah and the Gemara.

test.q: Where is Rashi's commentary printed on the standard page?
test.why: Rashi sits on the inner margin, next to the binding; Tosafot sit on the outer margin.
The Tosafists of the 12th–13th centuries included Rashi's grandsons and students.

test.q: What does the citation Berakhot 2a point to?
choices: The second tractate of the Talmud
test.why: Talmud citations name the tractate, the leaf (daf) and the side, a or b.

test.q: Who printed the first complete Talmud, in Venice in 1520–23?
test.why: Daniel Bomberg, a Christian printer, produced the first full printed Talmud in Venice.

choices: The Talmud edition printed in Vilna in 1880–86
test.why: The Romm press in Vilna printed the edition whose layout most students use today.

test.q: In a sugya, what is a kushya?
test.why: A kushya is a difficulty raised against a claim.

test.q: Which word shows that a question was left open?
"If this is true in the small case, how much more in the big case." Which tool is this?
test.why: Kal va-chomer argues from the lighter to the heavier case.

test.q: What did Hillel prove in Pesachim 66a using a gezerah shavah?
choices: The Passover offering may be made on the Sabbath
A worker may eat from the crop
test.why: Hillel linked "in its appointed season" in two laws to show the Passover offering overrides the Sabbath.
Tanu rabbanan signals a teaching of the tannaim from outside the Mishnah.

test.q: Which pair were first-generation Babylonian amoraim?
test.why: Rav and Shmuel taught in the early 200s CE, the first generation of Babylonian amoraim.

test.q: According to Bava Metzia 22b, in how many cases does the law follow Abaye over Rava?
test.why: The memory word Ya'al Kegam stands for the six cases.

test.q: Why does Mishnah Eduyot 1:5 record a minority view?
choices: To embarrass the rabbi who lost
So a later court may rely on it
test.why: Eduyot 1:5 says a lone view is kept so a later court may rely on it.

test.q: Which of these modern editions is a free online library of the Talmud?
test.why: Sefaria offers the Talmud online; the Vilna and Venice editions are printed books.

write.prompt: Does the Talmud care more about the answer or about the argument? Cite two or three passages from this unit, such as Berakhot 2a, Eruvin 13b, Mishnah Eduyot 1:5 or Bava Metzia 22b. Explain what each passage says and how different readers have understood it.
tips: Name the tractate and page for every passage you cite.
Say who is speaking: the Mishnah, the Gemara, a named rabbi, or a later reader.
Use the unit's terms, like sugya, kushya, terutz and teyku.
Compare readings without saying which one is true.
Point to what a ruling protects, such as a worker or a minority view.
